title: Deployment architecture for Next.js
description: Compare self-hosted, containerized, and platform deployments for Next.js and choose the right infrastructure strategy.

data.text: Deploying a Next.js app is not just 'push to production'. You must choose a **hosting model**, decide which rendering modes to support, and configure caching and image optimization. The three common paths are: **self-hosted Node.js**, **containerized deployment**, and **platform-as-a-service**.

Each path trades control for convenience. Self-hosted gives full infrastructure control but requires you to manage TLS, scaling, and CDN caching. Platforms like Vercel or Netlify handle most of that for you. Containers sit in the middle: portable, but still your responsibility to orchestrate.

rows: Full API compatibility and complex backends

data.title: Output modes
data.text: Next.js supports `output: 'standalone'` for self-hosted, `output: 'export'` for static hosting, and default server mode for platforms. Choose the mode that matches your hosting target before optimizing the rest.

data.title: Self-hosted with standalone output
data.content: Build a minimal server for self-hosted deployments.
data.code:
// next.config.js

/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  output: 'standalone',
};

module.exports = nextConfig;

# Dockerfile
FROM node:20-alpine AS base
FROM base AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json yarn.lock ./
RUN yarn install --frozen-lockfile

FROM deps AS builder
COPY . .
RUN yarn build

FROM base AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV production
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public

EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

data.title: Static export for CDN hosting
data.content: Build fully static HTML, CSS, and JS.

terms.definition: A build mode that bundles only the necessary server files for production.
A build mode that generates plain HTML files with no Node.js server required.
A network of servers that caches and serves static assets from locations close to users.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Use platforms for speed of deployment and built-in caching.
Use containers when you need reproducible infrastructure across environments.
Use static export when your app has no server-side data requirements.
data.takeaway: Your deployment architecture should match your team's operational skill and your app's performance requirements.
